title: Construction of a 18-Metal Neodymium(III) Nanoring with NIR Luminescent Sensing to Antibiotics

synthesis.procedure: At room temperature, triethylamine in 1 mL of MeOH (1.0 mol/L) was added to an EtOH solution (9 mL) of Nd(OAc)3·4H2O (0.20 mmol, 0.0640 g), H4L1 (0.20 mmol, 0.0756 g), and H2L2 (0.10 mmol, 0.0136 g). The mixed solution was heated under reflux for 30 min with stirring. Slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the solution at room temperature afforded pale red crystals of 1 after 1 week. Isolated yield 31% (0.0269 g) based on Nd(OAc)3·4H2O.

reagents.name: H4L1 (hexadentate salen-type Schiff base from 2,3-dihydroxybenzaldehyde and 4,5-dimethyl-1,2-phenylenediamine)

synthesis.temperature: room temperature addition, then reflux; crystallization at room temperature
synthesis.vessel_or_method: solution reflux followed by slow diethyl ether diffusion
synthesis.workup_and_crystallization: slow diffusion of diethyl ether into the reaction solution at room temperature; pale red crystalline material isolated after 1 week

properties.summary: In CH3CN, 1 shows NIR Nd(III) emission at 884, 1064, and 1337 nm upon 371 nm excitation (lifetime 6.44 μs at 1064 nm; ΦLn 2.58%; overall Φem 0.17%; sensitization efficiency 6.59%). It acts as a selective NIR luminescent sensor for nitrofuran antibiotics via inner-filter quenching, with KSV 1.4×10^4–3.5×10^4 M−1 and LODs 0.9–2.2 μM; selectivity is retained in the presence of other antibiotics.
